name: Text as a whole
title: REPORT on the proposal for a regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council on circularity requirements for vehicle design and on management of end-of-life vehicles, amending Regulations (EU) 2018/858 and 2019/1020 and repealing Directives 2000/53/EC and 2005/64/EC
part_text:
The report sets out Parliament's position on new EU rules for designing cars and handling vehicles when they are scrapped. It asks for recycled plastic targets in new cars (20 percent, later rising), rules on recycled steel and aluminium, easier removal of batteries and motors, and better tracking of scrapped cars. It also tightens conditions for exporting used vehicles and excludes classic cars, caravans and some special vehicles from the rules.

- New cars must contain more recycled plastic, steel and aluminium; manufacturers report on progress.
- Scrapyards, repairers and exporters face clearer duties; classic cars and caravans are exempt.
- Parliament's position now goes to talks with EU governments before the law is final.
